lens: story & curiosity: arc, stakes, emotion, pacing, memorable images, plants and payoffs
summary: The finale now works. In ch15-s09 the screen goes dark to a single cyan cursor pinprick (+15.79), which calls back the film's first frame. A neighbour's lamp is full by 'lamp' (17.21), the hand comes in on 'suspicious', and the flame catches on 'candles' (22.06), matching the foley flare (2127.56). The candle then holds clean for 2.5 s. The second through-line question is now carried visually: ch13-s01 pins HOW FAR? HOW FAST? on 'second' (22.04) beside WHO TAUGHT IT?, and ch15-s08 brings it back on 'how far' with a STATUS: OPEN stamp. 'Now, it found him' lands with Hinton already at the desk. The end cards are 22 s. The film's question ledger is complete: who taught it, who paid for dinner, why choose the fog, can a fence hold, how far and how fast, and the dark lantern. Each is either paid off aloud or deliberately left open. Its strongest quiet beats (Rosenblatt's dedication, 'A cliff.', Widrow's lantern) are intact. Four things keep story at 8.5. (1) The turn into the story, L0114, runs at 221 wpm, against the user's direction of 'plainly, at normal pace', so the hinge of the prologue is the fastest line in the film. (2) ch15-s06 still opens on a featured, silent Hassabis beat, although the ledger marks it fixed. (3) The ch15 present-day stretch (s01-s05, about 2:18) still reads like a news crawl. ch15-s05 is 41.7 s, its opening wide does not name the field, and the text trim was not applied. (4) The three-part STATUS: OPEN motif is only heard once: the ch15-s08 stamp is tiny and silent.

issues.problem: The film's hinge into history, 'Our story starts all the way back in World War Two.', runs 2.98 s for 11 words (3.70-6.68), about 221 wpm. That is the fastest line in the film; QA pacing FAILS and the median is 150. User direction (2026-10-13) is that it be said 'plainly at normal pace'. So the moment the film turns from the prologue's riddle to 1943 lands as a rushed aside, and the rewind montage (go stone, fans, snow, knob, lantern) under it has no time to breathe.
issues.fix: Re-take L0114 solo with the text unchanged and no respelling, at tts speed about 0.82-0.85 with the same neutral direction ('plain, unhurried, no excitement'). Target 3.8-4.2 s (about 160-175 wpm). Keep L0114b as is. ch01-s06 already anchors every beat with T.word ('starts', 'Two', 'Chicago'), so it absorbs the change; the ~1 s goes to the clock (6.46 s of headroom under the 2160 s ceiling). Hand m01 a re-fit of its reversed swell before 'Our'. Re-run STT and QA pacing on the line.

The first two stamps are silent, so the rule the ear should learn ('a clack means a question stays open') is taught only on its last use. The foley bus has room: 5 of a maximum of 10 events are used.

issues.problem: ch05-s01 plants a lovely orphan: Hopfield's Versailles talk, which he wrote that he 'never met anyone who remembered hearing'. Thirty-one minutes later the Nobel goes to 'John Hopfield' with no callback, and the sheet only captions him 'physicist, aged 91'. The film pays off nearly every other plant (Widrow, the dinner bet, the waiting note, Lenat's 'practically nothing'), so this one reads as a missed rhyme rather than a choice.
issues.fix: Revise L1502's opening clause to: 'A Nobel Prize in physics, shared with John Hopfield, whose Versailles talk, he wrote, nobody remembered hearing: for memories that roll downhill, and the Boltzmann machine Hinton co-invented, a net that settles as it cools.' [same claim as L0524b]. This adds about 2 s, within the 6.46 s of clock headroom (less L0114's retake). Re-narrate solo. ch15-s01 absorbs it through T.word; the JOHN HOPFIELD card can gain a second line, 'Versailles, 1981', on 'Versailles'.

issues.problem: There is a small story ambiguity at the very end. L1527 answers 'Who taught it?' outright ('Learning, with its accomplices... Never one person'), then ch15-s09 stamps the WHO TAUGHT IT? card STATUS: OPEN (+13.92). A first-time viewer can read that as the film taking its answer back. What is really open is how it works and how far it goes (the dark lantern and HOW FAR?), not who taught it.
issues.fix: Before the stamp, at about +12.3 in the silence after L1518, have the hand pin a small verdict slip beneath WHO TAUGHT IT?: 'LEARNING + ACCOMPLICES · NEVER ONE PERSON' (typewriter, 22 px cap or larger). Then stamp STATUS: OPEN across the case-file folder tab (the file from ch01-s04), not the question card itself. Keep the stamp on b3 so fx-stamp is unchanged. Alternative with no new text: stamp 'CASE STATUS: OPEN' (the chapter title) instead of 'STATUS: OPEN'.

best_moments: ch01-s01 to ch15-s09: the film opens on a lone cyan cursor in black and closes by returning to one, which then gives way to a lamp in a neighbour's window and a match struck on 'candles'. A true bookend.
ch01-s04 / L0109: the lamp clicks on, WHO TAUGHT IT? is pinned, and OpenAI's own first-day admission is filed. The case is open within 50 seconds.
ch02-s04 / L0209: 'Each belief gets one, burning as long as it was held.' One rule turns 80 years into a bar chart in wax, and it pays off in ch15-s08's 'some, two; one match, a day'.

ch04-s05: 'In 1971, on his forty-third birthday, Frank Rosenblatt drowned while sailing.' Then silence, as Perceptrons opens to the handwritten 'In memory of Frank Rosenblatt, second printing, 1972'. This is still the film's best quiet beat.
ch06-s05 to ch07-s01: 'So who paid for dinner? Keep that question.' ... 'Both men. Each man lost one bet.'

ch08-s13b: 'Why choose the fog?' The clean bowl gets stamped BY HAND, then the learned tiles snap out of the fog on 'cut' and stack into a tower on 'many layers deep'. Hinton, at the edge of the light for thirty-six years, is standing at the desk when the pool reaches him.
ch08-s12 / L0823: the error drops 10.9 points and the narrator says only 'A cliff.'
ch12-s06: 'Not a new engine. A new door.' The cyan box warms to amber, and the camera pulls back to one warm window in a city of cold ones.

ch13-s01: Hinton takes his own '30 TO 50 YEARS OR EVEN LONGER' slip off the Wall, and on 'second question' a hand pins HOW FAR? HOW FAST? beside WHO TAUGHT IT?. The film's second act question gets its own card.
ch14-s02 to ch14-s07: 'CAN A FENCE AROUND CHIPS HOLD?' hangs over the strait and comes back stamped STATUS: OPEN, answered honestly.
ch15-s07: Widrow's lantern in a snowy window, 'never got over it'. 'Remember him' is paid off 32 minutes after it was planted.
ch15-s08 / L1514: 'Never one person. The board was a network all along.' The case board rewires into lanterns, with one still dark.
